items.title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Re-Release With New Rosario Dawson Night Nurse Footage Sets Release
items.summary:
Sony will put an extended cut of Spider-Man: Brand New Day back in theaters on December 4, timed to the heart of awards season. The new version carries the title Spider-Man: [Brand New] Brand New Day, and tickets go on sale November 19.

The main addition is footage of Rosario Dawson as Night Nurse, a character she played across Marvel's television run in Daredevil, Iron Fist, Luke Cage and The Defenders. Dawson had already told interviewers she shot a scene for Destin Daniel Cretton's film that didn't make the theatrical cut. The re-release restores it along with other new material.

The film has little left to prove commercially. Since opening July 31, it has set the record for the biggest North American opening at $360 million and the biggest previews ever at $72 million, and it posted the second-largest global debut on record at $932 million. Its $959 million domestic total makes it the highest-grossing release ever in the U.S., and it ranks third worldwide all time.

The December return is tied to an Oscar campaign Sony confirmed to Deadline, which first reported the re-release plan. Tom Rothman, chairman and CEO of Sony Pictures Motion Picture Group, framed the push as an argument about what voters are willing to take seriously. "The Academy is meant to recognize greatness. So, to be honest, I think comes down to greatness," he said, adding the question he puts to people directly: "Are you telling me that there are 10 films this year that are better than this film?"

The first weekend of December usually cools off after the Thanksgiving rush and tends to belong to genre titles, with Universal's Violent Night 2 occupying that slot this year. Sony is betting that a re-cut version of the year's biggest film can hold its own there while keeping the Marvel Studios and Pascal Pictures production in front of awards voters.

items.title: Hayley Williams Curates Outbreak Fest 2027 Lineup Topped by American Football, Dinosaur Jr., Wednesday
items.summary:
Hayley Williams will headline both nights of Outbreak Fest 2027 in Manchester and has curated the festival's lineup. The Paramore singer is billed as The Hayley Williams Show across June 19th and 20th, with American Football, Dinosaur Jr. and Wednesday joining her at the top of the first announcement.

Thirty-four acts have been revealed so far, and the spread makes clear how far Outbreak has traveled from its hardcore and punk roots. Blood Orange, Julien Baker, Mannequin Pussy, Rico Nasty and former Modern Baseball co-vocalist and guitarist Bren Lukens all appear on the bill, pulling in alternative rock, hip-hop, R&B and electronic music.

The heavier end of the festival's history is still well represented. Soul Glo, H2O, Drain, Drug Church, PISS, Rival Schools and Spiritual Cramp are scheduled alongside Appleseed, ear, Failure, feeble little horse, Mary in the Junkyard and Sweet Pill.

Both single-day tickets and two-day passes go on sale from the outset, according to Consequence. Fans can register for the pre-sale through Tuesday, November 17th at midnight GMT, with codes sent out between 9:00 a.m. and 10:00 a.m. GMT on Wednesday, November 18th before the pre-sale opens at 10:00 a.m. that day. The general on-sale follows Thursday, November 19th at 10:00 a.m. GMT.

Organizers will donate £1 from every ticket sold, split evenly between Medical Aid for Palestinians and Not a Phase, and will collect donations on-site for the Manchester Central Foodbank. More artists are still to come, including a separate June 18th show, and weekend ticket holders will be able to upgrade once that announcement lands.

items.title: How ‘Twilight’ Predicted Robert Pattinson’s James Bond Casting
items.summary:
Robert Pattinson will play James Bond, a casting announced Monday that puts him in the role Daniel Craig left behind after 2021's No Time to Die. The decision ends a long search and hands 007 to an actor who first broke through as a vampire in a teen romance.

That earlier film is now getting a second look. In 2008's Twilight, Pattinson's Edward Cullen falls for Kristen Stewart's Bella Swan, and roughly halfway through the movie Bella's classmates debate a prom theme that turns out to be Monte Carlo. "Gambling, tuxedos, and Bond, James Bond," Eric, played by Justin Chon, says in the scene, as Christian Serratos' Angela reacts and the camera cuts to Edward smirking while he opens a car door for Bella.

The Hollywood Reporter had previously identified Pattinson as one of the finalists for the part, alongside Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Josh O'Connor and Nicholas Hoult. Director Denis Villeneuve and producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman settled on Pattinson.

"James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime," Pattinson said in a statement. "I'm deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn't be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team."

The Twilight franchise's official X account leaned into the coincidence after the news broke, posting the prom-theme clip with the caption, "It all comes back to Twilight." Pattinson, whose Edward once warned Bella he had "the skin of a killer," now has the license that goes with it.
